name: Zohar
overview: Zohar was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, identified specifically as a son of Simeon. He is noted in Scripture as one of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt during the patriarchal migration. The biblical record associates him with the Zerahites, a clan descending from him, highlighting his place in Israel's tribal history.
namesAndTitles: The name Zohar means "yellowish red" or "tawny," reflecting a descriptive Hebrew proper name. He is also referred to as Zerah, which means "dawning," "shining," or "flashing [red or scarlet] light," indicating a possible variation or alternate form of his name in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Zohar as a son of Simeon, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text concerning him.
scriptureSignificance: Zohar's significance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt, marking a key moment in Israelite history that set the stage for later developments in God's covenant people. As an ancestor of the Zerahites, he represents a foundational figure within the tribe of Simeon, contributing to the tribal organization and identity of Israel as recorded in the Pentateuch.
